t: Ascribed by tradition to Vyasa, the Mahabharata grew from an oral tale of bards into one of the longest epic poems known, its bulk probably compiled between the 3rd century BCE and the 3rd century CE.

It tells of the struggle between the Kaurava and Pandava cousins for the throne of Hastinapura, ending in the Kurukshetra War, and holds the Bhagavad Gita, a prominent sacred text in Hindu traditions.

Retold in Tamil, Kannada, Telugu, Bengali and many other languages, in Persian at Akbar's court and in Javanese, it lives on in drama, film, television and folk ritual, and the Gita helped inspire the Indian independence movement.
dyk: At about 1.8 million words, the Mahabharata is roughly ten times the length of the Iliad and the Odyssey combined.
ev: Panini's grammar, the Ashtadhyayi, gives the earliest known references to bharata and mahabharata, though whether it means the epic is uncertain
The bulk of the Mahabharata is probably compiled in these centuries
The text probably reaches its final form by the early Gupta period
A copper-plate inscription of Maharaja Sharvanatha from Khoh describes the epic as a collection of 100,000 verses
Faizi and ʽAbd al-Qadir Badayuni produce the Razmnameh, a Persian translation commissioned by the Mughal emperor Akbar
Kisari Mohan Ganguli's prose version, the first complete English translation, is published
Scholars at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in Pune produce the Critical Edition of the Mahabharata
B. R. Chopra's television series Mahabharat is broadcast on India's national television, Doordarshan

f.made: Traditionally ascribed to the sage Vyasa, himself a major figure in the epic; it began as an orally transmitted tale of charioteer bards and grew through several redactions, its bulk probably compiled between the 3rd century BCE and the 3rd century CE, its final form reached by the early Gupta period.
f.form: A Sanskrit epic, the Mahābhārata (“Great Bharata”), in 18 parvas or books, told as tales within tales; its longest version has over 100,000 shlokas (couplets), or over 200,000 lines, with long prose passages, about 1.8 million words in all.
f.where: Manuscripts from across India and abroad, the oldest surviving Sanskrit text dating to the Kushan Period; the Critical Edition of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Pune, on 13,000 pages in 19 volumes; translations and retellings in Tamil, Kannada, Telugu, Bengali, Persian, Javanese and many other languages.
f.known: the rivalry of the Kauravas and Pandavas; Draupadi; the dice game and the thirteen-year exile; the 18-day Kurukshetra War; the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna's teaching to Arjuna; dharmayuddha, the theory of just war; the stories of Shakuntala, of Savitri and Satyavan and of Damayanti
